The best free HTML to PDF converters

Turning HTML into a PDF is easy when the page is online and harder when it is a saved file with its own pictures. Here are five free converters: four online services and one that works in your browser without uploading the file.

We make Slop HTML to PDF, one of the tools on this page. Every fact about the other tools comes from their own pages, linked under each one, as they read on 2026-10-24. Prices and features change: check each site before you choose.

How we compared them

  • Free to use, and the limits of the free plan
  • Whether your HTML is uploaded to a server
  • What it takes: a web address, an HTML file, pasted code, pictures
  • Control over the page: size, orientation, margins, headers

1. Slop HTML to PDF (ours)

Best for: Saved HTML files, such as reports, receipts or exports, that should not leave your computer.

Good

  • The file is read in your browser; nothing is uploaded
  • Scripts and remote content are removed, and the preview loads nothing from the network
  • Attach the page’s pictures from your computer; they are matched by file name
  • A4, Letter, A5 or Legal, portrait or landscape, three margins, fit to width, background graphics
  • Optional header on every page with the name, the date and a QR code

Not so good

  • Cannot convert a web address: give it the HTML file or the code
  • Pages that need JavaScript to draw themselves will not look the same, because scripts are removed
  • The PDF is made by the browser’s print dialog (Save as PDF)
  • Still in beta

Open Slop HTML to PDF

2. PDF24

Best for: Turning a live web page into a PDF from its address, free and without limits.

Good

  • Free with no limits and no registration
  • Paste a URL and download the PDF
  • Works on any system and browser
  • PDF24 Creator, a free Windows app, works offline with files on your PC

Not so good

  • The web page is fetched and converted on PDF24’s servers
  • Its webpage-to-PDF page lists no page size or margin options
  • Advertising on the pages

PDF24 website · Sources: PDF24 Webpage to PDF, PDF24 Creator

3. iLovePDF HTML to PDF

Which one to choose

For HTML files on your computer, Slop HTML to PDF comes first: it is free with no limits, the file never leaves your browser, and you choose the paper, margins and a header. It cannot fetch a web address and it removes scripts, so a page that draws itself with JavaScript will not come out the same.

For a live web page, PDF24 is the simplest free choice with no limits, and iLovePDF gives the most layout control (screen width, one long page, ad removal). Sejda is fine for a few conversions an hour and has a desktop version. CloudConvert suits API and batch work within 10 free conversions a day.

Questions

Can I convert an HTML file to PDF without uploading it?

Yes. Slop HTML to PDF reads the file in your browser and prints it to PDF there. PDF24, iLovePDF, Sejda Web and CloudConvert convert on their own servers, and say they delete the files after one hour, two hours or straight after processing.

How do I turn a web page into a PDF from its address?

Paste the URL into PDF24’s Webpage to PDF, iLovePDF or Sejda. Slop HTML to PDF needs the page saved as an HTML file, or its code pasted in.

Why are the pictures missing from my PDF?

A saved HTML file often points to pictures in a folder beside it. In Slop HTML to PDF, add those pictures with Local images and they are matched by file name. Remote pictures on the web are not loaded.

Is there a free HTML to PDF converter without limits?

Slop HTML to PDF has no limits, and PDF24 says its tools have none. Sejda’s free service allows 3 tasks an hour, and CloudConvert’s free plan 10 conversions a day.
